title: Autumn Community Assembly: choose the next two projects
summary: Members will vote on the institute's next two projects on 26 September. Six proposals are on the table, from a repair café network to a Greater Region housing observatory.
body:
The Autumn Community Assembly takes place on Saturday 26 September at the Hollerich office and online. Members receive the six proposals one week in advance. Anyone can attend; members vote.

## Six proposals on the table

- A repair cafe network across three communes
- A Greater Region housing observatory
- A second Solidarity Wardrobe in Esch
- A youth cycling repair point
- An open dataset of municipal budgets
- A winter lecture series on cooperation

> The two selected projects begin in November with a small seed budget and a volunteer coordinator each.

## How the vote works

Each member has two votes. Proposals need a simple majority and at least one volunteer willing to coordinate. Results are published here the same evening.

If you are not yet a member, [join before the 20th](volunteer.html#community) and you can vote.
author: Helix Anthropis Institute

title: Open Knowledge Lab releases its first two prototypes
summary: A plain-language research summariser and a shared community indicator dataset are now available under open licences.
body: Both prototypes are published on the institute's repository with documentation and a short video walkthrough. The lab is looking for two municipalities willing to pilot the indicator dataset this autumn.

title: Common Ground Gardens opens its second season with three new plots
summary: Bonnevoie, Gasperich and Cents join the network. Forty households now share the growing calendar.
body:
The new plots were allocated after a spring call that received more than twice the applications the network could host.

Each plot group has agreed its own rules and a rota. A harvest evening for all plots is planned for late September.

## What changed since season one

- Shared tool libraries at every plot
- A written water plan agreed with the commune
- A monthly open evening for neighbours who are not growing

> Forty households now share the growing calendar.

title: Twelve student teams pitch their town projects
summary: The Youth Futures pitch evening drew municipal representatives from five communes. Three proposals received seed support.
body: Winning proposals included a youth-run bicycle repair point, a multilingual welcome guide for new residents, and a plan to reopen a disused school garden. Teams will present progress at the next Community Assembly.

title: The institute confirms its executive board for 2026 to 2028
summary: Martim Galésio, Giovanni De Brito and Mathieu Plaquevent will lead the institute for the next two years.
body: The board was confirmed at the Spring Community Assembly. Its priorities for the period are the Greater Region cooperation programme, the fellowship, and a stable membership base that can fund small projects quickly.

title: Field Notes: our new Substack
summary: Short, honest write-ups from inside our projects, twice a month.
body: Field Notes is written by the people running each project. It is free, and it is where we say what did not work as well as what did.
